chapters.category: Ethiopic textual tradition • Modern English research translation
chapters.title: Chapter 35 — The Three Western Gates
chapters.sourceNote: Translated afresh into clear modern English from the earliest complete primary-language witness available for this chapter. No extant Aramaic wording has been identified for 1 Enoch 35, and the surviving continuous Greek Codex Panopolitanus ends at 32:6. The complete Ethiopic (Geʽez) text preserved in Rylands Ethiopic MS 23 is therefore the translation base for this one-verse chapter. Its comparison between three western gates and the corresponding eastern gates is retained without adding functions not stated in this unit. No unattested wording was supplied, and no modern English translation was used as the translation base.

verses.text: From there I went westward to the ends of the earth and saw three gates of heaven standing open there, like the gates I had seen in the east: the same number of gates and the same number of outlets.
verses.study: The western boundary mirrors the east with three open gates and three corresponding outlets. The matching number emphasizes symmetry across the vision's directional survey. This chapter records the structural correspondence without assigning the western gates additional weather effects.
crossReferences: Genesis 1:14–18 — heavenly lights move within an ordered day-and-night arrangement
Psalm 19:4–6 — the sun's course spans the heavens from one end to the other
Isaiah 45:6 — east and west together testify that the LORD alone is God
1 Enoch 33:2–4 — eastern gates open for the ordered courses of the stars

explanation.heading: Chapter teaching and context
paragraphs: Chapter 35 is a single-verse transition from the northern gates to the west. Enoch sees three open heavenly gates whose number and outlets match what he saw in the east.

The chapter's theological emphasis is symmetry and order. Opposite boundaries are not disconnected realms; they participate in a corresponding arrangement. The same created world is governed across east and west.

Because the verse does not specify what passes through these western gates, the translation and study do not import details from neighboring chapters. Restraint preserves the chapter's actual contribution: a witnessed structural match.

The directional survey concludes in Chapter 36 with the southern and eastern winds. Chapter 35's compact western observation keeps that larger circuit moving while marking the balanced design of the heavenly boundaries.

crossReferences: Psalm 19:4–6 — the complete east-to-west course of the sun
Isaiah 45:6; Malachi 1:11 — east and west encompassed by God's name and rule
1 Enoch 33:2–4 — eastern gates and stellar outlets
1 Enoch 34:1–3 — three northern gates and their winds
